Rabeya Bhuiyan with Rafiqur Rahman Patwary, Nikhil Kumar Biswas and Shahanara Bhuiyan; Advocates ----- For the Convict-Petitioner
KM Zahid Sarwar, Deputy Attorney General with Monzu Naznin (Rosy), Assistant Attorney General ----- For the State.
parties:
Abul Hashem ----- Accused-Petitioner 
Vs.
State ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Shamsul Huda J: The instant rule was issued on 13-2 2007 calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order of convict and sentence dated 30-3-2005 passed by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Special Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka convicting the convict petitioner under section 9(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of taka 5,00,000 in default to suffer RI for 5 (five) years more in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Case No. 447 of 2000 should not be quashed and such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal, in short, are that the accused petitioner Md Abdul Hashem was implicated in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 447 of 2000 under section 9(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 arising out of Keranigonj PS Case No. 17 dated 16-5-2000. The petitioner after suffering in hajat for a considerable period obtained bail and he faced the trial but on the day of pronouncement of judgment he remained absent as a result the judgment was passed in his absence and thereafter he was arrested, as a result he could not file appeal in due time and, as such, he preferred the instant application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure upon which rule was issued. 

 3. It appears from the record that one Md Alauddin Bepari, son of Late Reaz Uddin Bepari, of village-Konoiyadda, Police Station-Bauphal, District-Patuakhali, A/P Modhyerchar, Police Station-Keranigonj, District Dhaka lodged FIR on 16-5-2000 with Keranigonj Police Station under section 9(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 stating inter alia that on 15-9-1999 his two minor daughters went to school at 10-00 AM and thereafter the infor-mant along with his wife left his house and went to visit their maternal aunt's house. The victim Mariam who was the eldest daughter of the informant, aged about 12 years was staying at home alone. In absence of her parents accused Abul Hashem aged about 55 years entered into their dwelling but and asked her regarding whereabouts of her father and mother, then she replied that they went to visit their material aunt's house. Suddenly Abul Hashem caught her and forcibly committed rape upon her showing fear of knife and threatened her not to disclose the occurrence to anybody. While his daughter became pregnant for 5 months, he himself and his wife created pressure upon Mariam who informed them that accused Abul Hashem has committed rape upon her, as a result she became pregnant. When Abul Hashem was asked, he created pressure to commit miscarriage of the pregnancy with an assurance that he would bear all the cost but they did not agree. Over this matter there was a Salish and accused Abul Hossain admitted his guilt in presence of Salish and assured that he would arrange marriage of the victim girl and he would bear all of the cost of the marriage. When he did not carry out the verdict of the Salish the informant lodged the FIR, and he put his LTI on the same. There was a written salishnama. 

 4. The Police investigated the case and submitted charge sheet No. 250 dated 6-7-2000 implicating the convict petitioner as sole accused. In the body of the charge sheet the fact of the FIR was almost re-iterated. It appears from the charge sheet that as Doctor did not hold any X-ray as a result the actual age of the victim could not be ascertained scientifically. It is further stated that during investigation the investigating officer came to know that at about 11-00 AM on 15-9-1999 in absence of other inhabitants of the house the petitioner entered into the house of the victim and pressed napkin (gamsa) in the mouth of the victim and showing fear of knife committed rape upon her and also threatened her not to disclose the occurrence. After observing of all legal formalities the case was transferred to the Court of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Bishesh Tribunal, Dhaka and the case was numbered as Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Case No. 447 of 2000. 

 5. In this case charge was framed under section 9(1) and 13(Ka)(Kha) and (Ca) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000. In the form of charge it is stated that on 15-9-1999 at about 10-00 AM the victim Mariam was raped by the accused petitioner by showing fear of knife and pressed her mouth and as a result she became pregnant and thereafter she gave birth to a female child. 

 6. In this case prosecution examined as many as 12 witnesses, but defence examined none. It appears from the trend of cross examination that the defence case, in short, is that the allegation made in the FIR is false, fabricated and the petitioner was falsely implicated in this case at the instance of his enemies who set fire at his house upon which he initiated a criminal case against them and some of the FIR named witnesses persons are accused of the said case, who managed to file this case after long lapse of time from the date of occurrence. 

 8. The story of disclosure of the above facts to her parents after lapse of 5 months pregnancy is also not humanly probable. It is usual that if any woman conceived the symptoms of pregnancy starts in her body from 2-3 months of pregnancy and it is positive case of the prosecution as it appears from the evidence that over the occurrence there was a Salish and in the Salish it was decided that the petitioner will have to pay Taka 35,000 as fine and on his failure to pay the said amount the case was initiated after lapse of about 8 months. 

 9. Learned Counsel further submits that in this case no independent corroborative witnesses have been examined, rather the evidence of the parents and the victim herself are self contradictory and full of embellishments. In fact, this case is of no evidence and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be quashed. 

 11. Learned Deputy Attorney General raised a question of law as to whether this Court is empowered to scan the evidence on record in a criminal miscellaneous case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as it is done in disposing of regular criminal appeal or not, inasmuch as the petitioner may invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in a case which is of no evidence and coram non-judice only. 

 12. In reply to the above submission, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that this Court has power to consider the evidence on record to ascertain as to whether the evidence on record is to be considered as to no evidence. Further she submits that the apex Court of this country has formulated some categories of cases where the High Court should interfere to quash the criminal proceeding and in the decision passed in the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs State, reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, the Appellate Division held that High Court should quash a criminal proceeding in the following cases: 

 3) That the allegations made against the accused persons do constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. In dealing with this class of cases it is important to bear in mind the distinction between a case where there is no legal evidence or where there is evidence which is manifestly and clearly inconsistent with the accusation made and cases when there is legal evidence which on its appreciation may not support the acquisition in question. 

 Reference may be made to 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16: The case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain. 

 Further reference may be made to the case of Mofazzal Hossain Mollah vs State, reported in 45 DLR (AD) 175, wherein it has been held tha t— 

 "The fact that the accused were tried and found guilty and then unsuccessfully filed an appeal and a revisional application cannot be a ground, in the facts of the present case (i.e. absence of any legal evidence), for refusing to exercise the Court's inherent power to secure the ends of justice by way of setting aside their conviction." 

 13. In short, it has been decided in many cases that although there are evidence against the accused, but if those evidence do not inspire confidence of Court to record conviction that will be treated as the case of no evidence. No evidence does not necessarily mean without evidence. 

 15. PW 1 stated in his examination-in-chief that on 15-9-1999 he went to bring his wife from her aunt's house after sending his 2 daughters to school and his son went to his shop for working and the youngest daughter Ayesha accompanied him towards his father-in-law's house. His daughter Mariam was alone at his house. On getting this occasion accused Abul Hashem committed rape upon his daughter showing fear of knife. While she was carrying for 5 months the informant and his wife created pressure upon her and then she disclosed that she was raped by Abul Hashem. While asked, Abul Hashem created pressure upon them to cause miscarriage of their daughter and he assured that he will bear all cost for such miscarriage and thereafter there was Salish and he promised to bear all cost for marriage of his daughter but thereafter he did not comply the verdict of the salish and there was written salish-nama. His daughter gave statement to the Magistrate, 1st Class on 22-5-2000 and she gave birth to a female child inside the jail and his daughter Mariam was residing in the safe custody of Mahila Ain Jibi Samity along with her daughter namely Mahua. He identified the accused on dock. The convict petitioner has two wives, 5 sons and 4 daughters. 

 16. In cross examination he stated that FIR was written by one Shamim who is inhabitant of Barisal. One Quayum and Hanif of his locality accompanied him the police station. He further stated that house of A Razzak Dewan is situated on the north side of his house who is a singer and “ঐ বাড়ীতে সর্বদা গানের আসর বসে।” Adjacent to his house the house of accused Hashem is situated. He sold a portion of his house to the brother of Hashem. During the regime of Awami League the house of the petitioner was burnt down by the local people for which he initiated a criminal case against some people. He further stated that he knew Modhu Miah, Mohiuddin, Moktar Hossain, Zinnah, Hanif and Nurunnobi, who are Murid of Charmonai Peer and he himself also Murid of Charmonai Peer Saheb and he could not tell whether any of the above persons is witnesses of this case. He came to know about the pregnancy of his daughter after lapse of 5 months, but his daughter could not tell the exact date of occurrence. Later on he said that the occurrence took place on 15-9-1999. He informed the matter to the local Union Parishad Member before lodging the FIR. He denied suggestion of the defence that he lodged the FIR at the instance of the accused of arson case of the house of the petitioner. There was. a Salish over the matter of pregnancy of his daughter. The salish held on Friday before Juma prayer. The Salish was held in between his house and the house of Hashem. He denied the suggestion that on that day there was measurement of his house due to boundary dispute between the accused and himself. He further denied the suggestion that he sold his entire house to the brother of Hashem and he being deprived of an opportunity to get permissive possession of the house this false case has been initiated. 

 17. PW 2 Noorjahan, wife of the informant Alauddin stated in her deposition that before 2/2-1/2 months of lodging the FIR she found that her daughter conceived and asked her as to who caused such pregnancy. She told that Abul Hashem committed rape upon her as a result she has conceived. On the date of occurrence she along with her husband and a child went to his aunt's house and sent female childs to school. The accused committed rape upon her daughter getting her alone in the house. The accused proposed to cause miscarriage, but they denied. Over the aforesaid dispute there was salish and the salishder gave verdict against the accused and directed to pay a fine of Taka 35,000 and on his failure to pay the fine her husband lodged the FIR. Her daughter give birth to a female child in jail and they are still in the custody of the Mahila Ain Jibi Samity. She denied the suggestion that she was previously married with Hasan Howlader and after divorce she was married with the informant. She stated that Mariam became adult and then she was aged 12 years. She could not tell how many times the boundary of her house were measured. She admitted that before 2/3 years they sold 1/2 katha land to Hatem Ali who is brother of accused Abul Hashem. She denied the defence suggestion that there was enmity over selling of the homestead land. She further denied the suggestion that they received money from Hashern through a Baina-nama for selling their homestead land to him. She had first came to know that while her daughter was carrying 2½/3 months and informed the matter to one Ataul Doctor, then said Doctor and the accused asked them to put signature on a paper for causing miscarriage, but they denied. The house of Badsha is situated after the house of Hashem. Said Badsha took her daughter Mariam to the house of maternal grandfather's house before 8/9 years back. She denied the suggestion that before 3-4 months back Badsha took her daughter Mariam to the house of her grandmother's house and thereafter she came back and there was free mixing with Mariam and Badsha. She categorically denied the suggestion that out of enmity the matter was set against the convict petitioner. She has 4 daughters and one son and Mariam is her 2nd daughter. In between her first ministration and before passing of second ministration this occurrence took place. She enquired to Mariam as to why her second ministration was stopped, but she did not tell anything, rather after passing of 5 months she became sure that her daughter was pregnant. 

 18. PW 3 Mariam, aged about 13 years. She stated that she is the victim of this case and the informant is her father. On 15-9-1999 the occurrence took place. On that day her parents went to her maternal grandfather's house. She herself was cooking in the house. At about 10.00 AM accused Abul Hashem came and enquired regarding his father and mother. She replied that they are not in the house, then he shut down the door of the house and committed rape upon her by putting gamsa in her mouth and while he was retreating he threatened that if she disclose the fact to anybody she would be murdered, as a result she could not disclose the fact to anybody. While she became pregnant for 5 months then her vomiting started and on query of her mother she disclosed the fact to her parents. Her father convened a salish over the matter and salishders imposed Taka 35,000 fine against the accused petitioner and on his failure to pay the money the informant lodged the FIR. She further stated that while she was in jail custody on 3-6-2000 she gave birth to a female child. She made statement before the Magistrate which was proved by her and marked as Exhibit 2 and her signature was marked as Exhibit 2/1. On 25-5-2000 she was medically examined. In cross examination she stated that after initiation of the Criminal Case she is staying in the Shelter Centre of the Mahila Ain Jibi Samity. Then she said that before giving birth to her child she was in jail custody. While she was in jail custody she has given statement to the Magistrate. She denied suggestion that she did not tell the date of occurrence to the investigation officer. She further stated that the name of her younger sister is Kulsum. She was married but she could not tell name of her husband. She could not tell the English month of the date 15-9-1999. Her younger sister did not tell the matter of her marriage to her parents. Kulsum is younger than her by 3-4 years. She stated that they have a tin-shed chapra with fencing made of bamboo and there is only one door in the house and there is no window in the said house and the kitchen house is separate. Her brother got married without the knowledge of her parents. She categorically stated that the date of occurrence has been mentioned in the FIR by her father. But she could not remember whether he told the date of occurrence to her father or not. The house of Abul Hashem is situated by the side of their house and nearby to their house there are houses of Motaleb and Badsha. She heard that accused Hashem has 10 sons and daughter. Amongst other she categorically told that, After 2-3 months of the occurrence she was feeling vomiting tendency, but she did not disclose the fact even to her mother. She further stated that accused committed rape upon her by tying her mouth and hand with Gamsa, 

 It means that she re-affirmed that she was making flower on the Shari before the occurrence. She could not tell whether any of the accused persons of the case of Hashem are witness of this case. Her parents were present in the Salish. She again stated that, “হাত ও মুখ বেধে ধর্ষনের কথা মা বাবাকে বলেছি কি না স্মরণ নেই।” She denied the suggestion that he deposed falsely. 

 ওয়ার্ড মেম্বার হাফিজ, মধু মিয়া, ছিদ্দিক ব্যাপারী, হযরত আলী, করিম আলী লোকজন সহ ১০/১২ জন বিচারক মন্ডলী ছিল। ৩৫,০০০/- টাকা শালিশে জরিমানা করার কথা আই/ও কে বলি নাই। শালিশের কোন কথাই বলি নাই, সেও জিজ্ঞাসা করে নাই।Some days before this occurrence the house of the petitioner was burnt for which he initiated a criminal case in which Modhu Haji and some others were accused. In cross-examination he stated that Salish was held in the house of Razzak Dewan. He denied the suggestion that there was no Salish in the house of Razzak Dewan. She further stated that in the Salish there was a written Salishnama, but he could tell that whether the Salishnama was given to the I/O or not. He denied the suggestion that there was no written Salishnama. He further denied the suggestion that he being influenced by the informant and he deposed falsely in this case. 

 23. PW 7 Hafiz Uddin stated in his examination-in-chief that he is Member of Ward No. 1 of Sagta Union Parishad. In the first part of 2000 (AD) informant Alauddin informed him that accused Abul Hashem committed rape upon his daughter Mariam as a result she became pregnant. Thereafter a Salish held and in the Salish accused petitioner was found guilty and he was directed to pay Taka 35,000 as fine. That amount of money was deposited to Salishder Yusuf Miah and after Salish a Salishnama was written on a stamp paper. He put his signature in the Salish-nama. He produced the Salish-nama which was marked as Exhibit 1 and his signature was marked as Exhibit 1/1. Thereafter as Manabadhikar Song-stha did not accept the complaint of the informant said Taka 35,000 was returned by Yusuf Miah to the informant. He stated in his cross-examination that I0 interrogated him at the last part of 2000 (AD) and he informed the 10 about the Salish over the matter. He denied the defence suggestion that imposing of fine against the petitioner and writing of stamp and depositing the money to Yusuf and Hazrat All and lodging the complaint to the Manabadhikar Songstha all are false and fabricated. He categorically stated that when stamp was written the accused person was not present there. He further stated that he put his signature on the stamp on the day of Salish but he did not put any date under his signature, but 2000 was written therein. He further told that he paid money to purchase stamp but he could not tell in whose name it was purchased. He denied the suggestion that the stamp was written for the requirement of the case. 

 24. PW 8 Dr Habibuzaman Chowdhury, Assistant Professor, Forensic Medicine, Dhaka Medical College, Dhaka stated in his examination-in-chief that on 30-5-2000 he was serving in Sir Salim Ullah Medical College Hospital in the Mid Ford. He examination Mariam with reference of Keranigonj PS Case No. 17 dated 16-5-2000 and after her examination the certificate was issued which was produced and marked as Exhibit 2 and his signature was marked as Exhibit 2/1. After examination he opined that, on the day of examination the victim Mariam, daughter of Alauddin was running 35 weeks pregnancy. On that day her age could not be estimated as X-ray could not be done as so is contra-indicated. 

 26. PW 10 Md Jahangir Hossain. He is retired Jail Superintendent. He stated in examination-in-chief that on 12-6-2000 he was serving as Senior Jail Super in Dhaka Central Jail. On 22-5-2000 he received victim Mariam in connection with Keranigonj PS Case No. 17 (5) 2000 and she was identified as Hajoti No. 10038/2000. She was carrying 8 months pregnancy. On 3-6-2000 she gave birth to a female child which was written in the Minute Book by a Doctor and subsequently it was sent to Magistrate, 1st Class, through Memo No. 4615, the Memo was marked as Exhibit 5 and his signature therein marked as Exhibit 5/1. In cross examination he stated that he himself saw the victim and her daughter. 

 27. PW 11 Sulekha Rani Basu, who was Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka Collectorate Bhaban, Dhaka. She recorded the statement of victim Mariam in connection with Keranigonj PS Case No. 17 dated 16-5-2000 and which was marked as Exhibit 6 and her signature was marked as Exhibit 6/1. She stated that she recorded the statement and the victim put his signature knowing the contents of the same. In cross-examination he stated that the victim did not tell about her age. She did not ascertain the truth about the occurrence but she just recorded her statement. 

 28. PW 12 Md Rafiqul Islam, SI of Police. He was PSI at the relevant time in the Keranigonj Police station. He was entrusted with the investigation of the case. He visited the place of occurrence and prepared the sketch map with index which was marked as Exhibit 7 and Exhibit 7/1 is his signature. He examined the witnesses and recorded the same. He stated that he sent the victim to the Magistrate for recording her statement and at that relevant time the victim was carrying 35 weeks pregnancy. After holding investigation he submitted charge sheet under section 9 (1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000. 

 29. In cross examination he stated that on 16-5-2000 at about 22-05 hours he received the case for investigation. He visited the place of occurrence on 17-5-2000 and prepared the sketch map. At the place of occurrence there was no other house except the house of the informant. The house of the accused is situated at a distance of 500 yards from the house of the informant. But there is a house of one of the witness of this case which is situated at a i distance of ½ km. He did not visit the house of the Khala Shashuri of the informant and did not ask anybody from that house. He categorically stated that the alleged occurrence took place on 15-9-1999 but the FIR was lodged on 16-5-2000. No alamats of rape was produced before him. He did not get any evidence as to whether the victim was treated by any Doctor at the relevant time. He categorically stated that Hafizuddin Member did not tell him that there was a Salish under his leadership and Taka 35,000 was awarded against the petitioner as fine or it was written in a stamp paper or he has signed the same. He could not tell that whether the victim gave birth to a female child on 3-6-2000 although he submitted charge sheet on 6-7-2000. He denied the suggestion that he did not examine any witness or did not conduct investigation properly. 

 32. PW 1 stated that they came to know about the pregnancy of their daughter while she was carrying for 5 months. On the other hand PW 2 stated that she came to know about the pregnancy after expiry of 2½/3 months and she was brought to Awal Doctor who advised them to cause miscarriage, but they did not agree. PW 3 the victim herself stated that while she was carrying for 5 months the matter was disclosed to her parents. PW 4 Doctor Ataul Haq stated that on 3rd March, 2000 the victim told him that she was raped by Abul Hashem and she was carrying pregnancy and there was a Salish over the matter while the victim was pregnant for 2 months. PW 5 Moktar Hossain stated that while the Salish was held the victim was carrying 8 months pregnancy PW 6 Nittanandon also stated that she was carrying 8 months pregnancy at the time of Salish. PW 7 Hafiz Uddin, so-called Salishder and Member of the Union Parishad stated in his examination-in-chief that at the first part of 2000 the informant informed him that the accused committed rape upon his daughter and as a result she became pregnant. After some days there was a Salish over the occurrence PW 8. Dr Md Habib-uz-zaman Chowdhury stated in his examination-in-chief that on 30-5-2000 he examined the victim in connection with Keranigonj PS Case No. 17 dated 16-5-2000 and ascertained that the victim was running 35 weeks of pregnancy, 35 weeks means more than 8 months. PW 10 Md Jahangir Hossain, Senior Jail Super, Dhaka Central Jail, Dhaka, stated in his examination-in-chief that on 22-5-2000 he received the victim in connection with the aforesaid case and she was hajoti No. 10038/00, then she was carrying for 8 months. On 3-6-2000 she gave birth of a female child. If we compare the above evidence of the prosecution witnesses it can be safely held that nobody told the exact date or approximate date of pregnancy of the victim girl, as well as the date of occurrence of commission of rape is imaginary, inasmuch as if we believe that Salish was held under the leadership of PW 7 Hafizuddin, the so-called Salish was held in the first part of 2000. In cross examination he stated that a Salish-nama was written on a stamp paper valued Taka 150 and it was written in the Salishnama “২০০০ সালের মার্চ মাসে শালিশ হয়।” If we believe his evidence it corroborates the evidence of other PWs, who stated that the victim girl was carrying for about 7-8 months and, as such, the alleged date of occurrence i.e. 15-9-1999 is an imaginary date and the question arises whom do we believe as regards the pregnancy of the victim girl? Mother of the victim stated that she learnt about the pregnancy after lapse of 2-3 months, then question arises why she did not tell her husband or anybody else, but apparently after lapse of 8 months the matter was disclosed. Here a serious doubt has been cropped up as to commission of rape by the accused and as regards conciseness of the victim as a result of rape alleged to have been committed on 15-9-1999. 

 34. He stated in his cross examination that Salish held in between his house and the house of Abul Hashem, the accused and it was held on Friday before Jumma prayer. On this point PW 4 stated that Salish was held in the house of one Razzak Dewan. Razzak Dewan was also present in the Salish and Salishnama was written by the Salishders. It may be mentioned here that Razzak De-Wan was not examined as witness in this case. PW 5 stated that Salish held at 11-00/12-00 AM but he could not remember the date of Salish and he further stated that as many as 500 people were present in the Salish. PW 6 Nittanandon stated on this point that Salish held at 3-00 PM but he mentioned no date. He further affirmed in cross-examination that Salish continued from 3-00 PM to 5-00 PM but the victim was not present in the Salish. Some juries were present but nobody was cited in the case as witness. PW 7 Hafizuddin, the Salishder and the Member of the Ward of the Union Parishad stated a new story. There was a Salish (no date and time), stamp paper was written in the Salish and accordingly Taka 35,000 was deposited with one Yunus Miah by the accused. The Salish-nama was exhibited as Exhibit 1 and his signature was marked as Exhibit 1/1 (with objection). In his cross-examination he candidly admitted that he did not put any date under his signature on the stamp paper and the stamp paper was purchased with his money. But he cannot tell who wrote the stamp paper and at the time of writing the stamp paper the accused petitioner was not present there. 

 38. Although the FIR is not a substantive piece of evidence but it is a valuable piece of evidence. The Court call take notice of any variation, deviated and embellishment of the FIR story. The FIR itself is a belated FIR without any explanation Inspite of that no where it was written that the accused committed rape upon the victim by putting gamsa in her mouth or trying her hands with gamsa. Certainly the PW 3 made embellishment to make the case believable but she make the case unbelievable as she stated that, “আমার মুখে গামছা দিয়ে ধর্ষন করে। পৃথক গামছা দিয়ে হাত বাধে পিটমোড়া করে। আগে মুখ ও পরে হাত বাধে।” 

 41. It may be mentioned here that the investigating officer stated in his cross examination that he went to the place of occurrence and found no house around the house of the informant and there is a house of a witness situated at a distance of 1½KM and he did not examine any neighbouring witness, nor so-called aunt of the wife of the informant or anybody from their house to ascertain the fact that at the relevant date and time the parents of the victim had been there or not, but conducted a perfunctory investigation and submitted charge sheet against the accused and the trial was held on such perfunctory investigation of the IO. In this regard learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there are gulf of difference between sexual intercourse and that of rape. Sexual intercourse may occur with consent where there is no chance of causing any injury over the body, but invariable where rape is committed there must be some resistance which creates marks of injury or violence over the body of the victim as observed by imminent Medical Jurist Modi. In this regard the learned Counsel for the petitioner referred to a decision of the case of Abdul Aziz vs State, reported in 2 BLC, 630. Wherein it has been held that— 

 She has referred to another decision. The case of Mohammad Abdul Klaleque vs State, reported in 12 DLR (SC) 165. 

 "In a case of this kind where the evidence and conviction of the prosecutrix form the only evidence which the Court has to go upon, it is necessity in order to sustain a convict, that it should at least be found that the woman's statement is in accordance with all the probabilities and has all the appearances of having been honesty made." 

 She has referred to another decision. The case of Shan Khan vs State, reported in 18 DLR (WP) 91. 

 Held: "In the case of rape, according to Modi's Medical jurisprudence the body, specially the face, breasts, chest, lower part of abdomen, limbs and back should have marks of violence such as scratches and bruises, as a result of struggle. Such marks are likely to be found on the bodies of grown up women who are able to resist." 

 43. The learned Judge of the Tribunal did not at all consider the attending circumstance, as revealed in the cross-examination by the defence, inasmuch as belated disclosure of fact of rape and belated examination of witnesses by the Investigating Officer resulting the prosecution case unbelievable, even then the learned Tribunal convicted the accused causing miscarriage of Justice. 

 44. Judgment of conviction or acquittal cannot be passed or recorded on hypothesis, it must be based on evidence of unimpeachable character, which are very much absent from this case, as we have categorically discussed above with reference to the evidence of the prosecution witnesses. 

 45. Regarding abscontion of the accused on the date of pronouncement of judgment has been consider as his guilty mind. But it is unsafe to find an accused guilty of the offence or his mere absconding inasmuch as it may happen due to misconception or ill advice of his lawyer or lawyer's clerk and sometimes it may happen due to the situation which was beyond his control. 

 In this regard the learned Counsel has referred to a decision: The case of State vs Badshah Mollah, reported in 41 DLR 11. 

 46. From the discussions made above we hold that the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the case beyond any reasonable doubt, rather this case is based on hypothesis, conjecture and full of doubt. In our foregoing discussions herein made above we have categorically discussed the evidence and found it difficult to uphold the judgment and order of conviction and sentence, inasmuch as neither the date of occurrence nor the place of occurrence, manner of occurrence place of Salish, date and time of Salish, violation of the order of Salish and admission of guilt by accused have been proved by reasonable and believable testimonies and, as such, we are constrained to hold that although there is evidence but this evidence creates serious doubt over the prosecution case and creates no credence in the mind of Judge of this Court and, as such, this is treated as a case of no evidence. 

 47. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 30-3-2005 passed by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Special Tribunal No.1, Dhaka convicting the convict petitioner under section 9(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Doman Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 5,00,000 in default to suffer RI for 5(five) years more in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Case No. 447 of 2000 is set aside. 

 Let the accused petitioner Md Abul Hashem, son of Late Hasmat Ali, of village-Maddher Char (Ali), Police station- Keranigonj, District- Dhaka be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted with any other case.
